title: Architecture diagram nodes
content: Interactive architecture diagram nodes: Org/Team/User scopes every query to the org graph. FastAPI handles auth, routing, and SSE streaming. Hybrid + Graph RAG fuses dense and sparse search with graph hops. Qdrant stores embeddings. LLM providers generate answers with retrieved chunks in context.

title: Recent build log
content: Recent work: portfolio rebuild with Next.js and glass design tokens; CompanyBrain Graph RAG chat path hardening with SSE and retrieval provenance; factory attendance report edge cases; WorkBuddy approval workflows and execution receipts that distinguish applied changes from verified results.

title: CompanyBrain — architecture
content: CompanyBrain architecture: Org/Team/User context hits a FastAPI orchestration layer. Hybrid search and graph RAG retrieve from Qdrant; the model stream returns over SSE while the UI surfaces retrieved chunks, confidence, and routing so operators can inspect why an answer was produced. Flow: Org → FastAPI → Hybrid + Graph RAG → Qdrant and LLM providers.

title: CompanyBrain — what broke
content: Early CompanyBrain prompts answered fluently while citing the wrong chunk. The fix was not a bigger model — it was forcing retrieved chunk metadata into the UI and scoring path so bad retrieval became visible. Also underestimated how much admin and observability UI a trusted chat product needs.

title: CompanyBrain — context
content: Built for teams that need an internal assistant grounded in their own documents and org graph. Constraints: solo-built product surface against a FastAPI backend; must stream answers with thinking/token separation and visible retrieval provenance; hybrid search plus graph RAG over a vector store; observability (latency, routing, hallucination forensics) is first-class.

title: CompanyBrain — decisions
content: Key decisions: (1) Hybrid search plus graph over vector-only — pure dense retrieval missed org-structure questions like who owns X on a team. (2) SSE streaming with thinking separation so the UI can show retrieval and reasoning stages live. (3) Qdrant instead of a managed mega-stack for predictable latency and cost at enterprise-doc scale.

title: CompanyBrain — problem
content: CompanyBrain addresses enterprise knowledge trapped across docs, tickets, and tribal memory. The goal is an internal assistant that answers with citations, not vibes — grounded in the company's own documents, org graph, and policies.

title: Factory Attendance — architecture
content: Capture devices on the floor feed a recognition pipeline; verified punches land in a cloud attendance store; ops get daily reports and exception queues instead of spreadsheets. The hard part is shift-change failure modes, not the model alone. Stack: face recognition, edge to cloud, ops tooling, reports.

title: Factory Attendance — what broke
content: Lighting and angle changes at real entrances killed early match rates that looked fine in controlled tests. Had to redesign capture guidance and fallbacks (retry, supervisor override). Learned that live means on-call for the first weeks of shift changes — documentation alone is not a handoff.

title: Factory Attendance — context
content: Built for a manufacturing site that needed reliable daily attendance without clipboard chaos or buddy-punching. Constraints: production environment where downtime is serious; varied lighting and shift-change queues; reports ops and payroll can use; solo delivery with clear handoff for on-site staff. Status: live in production.

title: Factory Attendance — decisions
content: Optimized for shift-change latency, not demo accuracy — a slow queue is a failed product. Ambiguous punches go to a human exception queue instead of silent auto-approve. Reports were a first-class surface early, not a CSV bolt-on at the end.

title: Factory Attendance — production proof
content: The factory attendance system is live in production: daily punches, reports, and exception queues on a real factory floor. It is one of the strongest proof points that Jayanth ships systems used by real operators, not demos.

title: Factory Attendance — problem
content: Factory Attendance automates attendance at manufacturing scale. Manual attendance is slow, error-prone, and painful to reconcile at payroll time. The system uses facial recognition on the factory floor with reports and exception handling.

title: This portfolio's RAG
content: This portfolio site itself runs a live RAG pipeline over Jayanth's case studies and resume. Ask My Work retrieves curated chunks with cosine similarity over precomputed embeddings, then streams an answer with clickable source chips. It demonstrates production RAG skill instead of only describing it.

title: WorkBuddy — architecture
content: Telegram and a native macOS companion share a FastAPI backend. SQLite stores plans, memory and task events; BM25 retrieves project documents. LangGraph pauses proposals for approval, then a model-free executor applies approved changes in isolated Git worktrees.

title: WorkBuddy — context
content: WorkBuddy is a local engineering companion for developers returning to a project. It combines project understanding, saved plans and memory with reviewable AI-proposed code changes, through Telegram and a native macOS companion.

title: WorkBuddy — decisions
content: Bind approval to the exact change: Bind the proposal hash, canonical project root, target paths, branch and base commit before the approval pause. Recheck the baseline around execution so an approval cannot silently authorize a different proposal. Keep the working checkout separate: Apply changes in a dedicated review worktree and stage only approved paths. Check the commit parent and tree before reporting success. Retain failed or partial worktrees for inspection; do not automatically merge or switch the source checkout. Record outcomes without inventing verification: Typed per-change and batch receipts distinguish applied, refused, partial and failed outcomes. Failed batches do not feed success-memory extraction. Execution receipts explicitly say verified: false until an integrated verification gate exists.

title: WorkBuddy — metrics
content: The local status document dated 23 September 2026 reports 547 core tests and 136 desktop tests passing, with 7 GUI tests skipped. Those results were not rerun for this portfolio update. Live model paths, Telegram delivery and end-to-end reliability are not established by those counts. Working local prototype; no production adoption or customer outcomes claimed. No integrated test-verification gate in the execution workflow yet. The desktop companion does not provide screen context or voice input. Shared Git metadata, concurrent changes and source freshness remain reliability work.

title: WorkBuddy — what-broke
content: The execution workflow needed a clearer distinction between a completed task and proven correctness. Typed receipts now preserve partial and failed outcomes, while the missing integrated test gate remains explicit. This is a documented reliability gap, not a claim of production readiness.
